understand.concept: Java is a general-purpose programming language used to build many kinds of software, including command-line tools, backend services, desktop applications and Android-related development workflows. This course begins with the Java language itself: source structure, values, control flow, classes, objects and libraries. Later modules cover exceptions, collections, threads, lambdas and file handling.
understand.whyItMatters: Learning Java provides a foundation for reading APIs, debugging programs and evaluating frameworks without confusing a framework with the language itself.
understand.analogy: Think of the course as a map: early lessons teach the symbols and routes, while later lessons combine them into larger journeys and applications.
understand.analogyLimit: A map is not the journey itself. Real programs involve design decisions, testing, dependencies, runtime configuration and maintenance.

explain.narrative:
## The Java learning path

This course follows the current W3Schools Java syllabus sequence. It starts with the language and development setup, then moves through variables and data types, control flow, arrays and methods, object-oriented Java, input and collections, exceptions and concurrency topics, and file handling.

## What Java is used for

Java is a general-purpose language. It is used in backend services, enterprise systems, tools, desktop software and Android development ecosystems. The right technology depends on project requirements; Java itself does not automatically provide every framework or platform feature.

## How you will practise

You will read original explanations, inspect complete Java examples, solve tasks and answer topic-specific questions. Java examples will be compiled and executed by a JDK in validation. The existing browser playground is designed for HTML, CSS and JavaScript, so Java lessons will not falsely claim that those snippets run in that editor.

## Course conventions

- Course ID: `java`; first module: `JV1`.
- English is the canonical authoring language for this phase.
- Every lesson uses Understand, Explain and Practise stages.
- Java source examples target a documented JDK baseline; vendor and version differences are called out where relevant.
